title: American Places – Gettysburg, Pennsylvania
titleZh: 美国名胜 – 宾夕法尼亚州葛底斯堡
credits: Nancy Steinbach and Ashley Thompson with additional material from the National Park Service for VOA Learning English. Mario Ritter, Jr. adapted it for the VOA Learning English podcast.

sentences.en: The Gettysburg National Military Park is in the small town of Gettysburg in the eastern state of Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 盖蒂兹堡国家军事公园位于东部宾夕法尼亚州的小镇盖蒂兹堡。

sentences.en: Much of the area around Gettysburg still looks like it did in the 1860s, during the American Civil War.
sentences.zh: 盖蒂兹堡周边的大片地区至今仍保留着19世纪60年代美国内战时期的模样。

sentences.en: The town is in the middle of good farmland.
sentences.zh: 这座小镇坐落于肥沃的农田中央。

sentences.en: Roads pass through Gettysburg that lead to Baltimore, Washington, D.C., and other eastern cities.
sentences.zh: 有通往巴尔的摩、华盛顿特区以及其他东部城市的道路穿过盖蒂兹堡。

sentences.en: It is hard to believe that two huge armies fought there.
sentences.zh: 很难相信曾有两支庞大的军队在这里交战。

sentences.en: One fighting force was the United States Army of the Potomac, commanded by General George Meade.
sentences.zh: 其中一方是由乔治·米德将军指挥的美国波托马克军团。

sentences.en: The other was the Confederate Army of Northern Virginia led by General Robert E. Lee.
sentences.zh: 另一方是由罗伯特·李将军指挥的南方邦联北弗吉尼亚军团。

sentences.en: Lee’s troops had moved north into Pennsylvania from Virginia.
sentences.zh: 李的部队从弗吉尼亚向北推进到了宾夕法尼亚。

sentences.en: Lee believed that a Southern win of a battle on Northern land would force a negotiated settlement of the Civil War and mean independence for the Confederate States.
sentences.zh: 李认为，南方在北方土地上赢得一场战役的胜利，将迫使对内战进行谈判解决，并使美利坚邦联获得独立。

sentences.en: The battle of Gettysburg began on July 1, 1863.
sentences.zh: 盖蒂兹堡战役于1863年7月1日打响。

sentences.en: About 170,000 soldiers fought for three days.
sentences.zh: 约有17万名士兵作战了三天。

sentences.en: When it ended on July 3, more than 50,000 soldiers were dead, wounded or missing.
sentences.zh: 当7月3日战斗结束时，已有5万多名士兵阵亡、受伤或失踪。

sentences.en: Lee’s army lost the battle.
sentences.zh: 李的部队在这场战役中失败了。

sentences.en: The museum also houses the Gettysburg cyclorama painting.
sentences.zh: 博物馆还展出了盖蒂兹堡全景画。

sentences.en: This kind of artwork completely surrounds the people looking at it.
sentences.zh: 这类艺术品将观看者完全环绕其中。

sentences.en: The painting shows the artist’s vision of the final major attack of the battle on July 3, 1863.
sentences.zh: 这幅画描绘了艺术家眼中1863年7月3日这场战役最后主要进攻的场景。

sentences.en: Over time, it has come to be called Pickett's Charge.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，它逐渐被称为皮克特冲锋。

sentences.en: George Pickett was one of several Confederate commanders ordered to make the charge.
sentences.zh: 乔治·皮克特是受命发动这次冲锋的几位邦联指挥官之一。

sentences.en: The Confederate soldiers reached a point close to the northern lines and headquarters.
sentences.zh: 邦联士兵推进到了距离北方战线和指挥部很近的一处地点。

sentences.en: Today, the point is called the “High Water Mark.”
sentences.zh: 今天，这个地点被称为'最高点'。

sentences.en: Northern forces then turned the Confederates back.
sentences.zh: 北方部队随后将南方邦联军队击退。

sentences.en: The charge failed.
sentences.zh: 这次冲锋失败了。

sentences.en: Southern forces would never again reach so far north.
sentences.zh: 南方部队此后再未能推进到如此偏北的地方。

sentences.en: Soon after the battle, people began to visit Gettysburg to try to understand what happened there.
sentences.zh: 战斗结束后不久，人们开始前往葛底斯堡，试图理解在那里发生的一切。

sentences.en: One of those visitors, on November 19, 1863, was President Abraham Lincoln.
sentences.zh: 其中一位访客便是亚伯拉罕·林肯总统，时间是1863年11月19日。

sentences.en: He was invited to help dedicate a burial ground for Union soldiers killed in the battle.
sentences.zh: 他受邀为一场战役中阵亡的联邦士兵墓地主持启用仪式。

sentences.en: Lincoln spoke for just two minutes.
sentences.zh: 林肯的演讲只持续了两分钟。

sentences.en: But his speech, known as “The Gettysburg Address,” is one of the most famous pieces of American oratory.
sentences.zh: 但他的这场演说，即《葛底斯堡演说》，成为美国乃至世界最著名的演讲之一。

sentences.en: I'm Mario Ritter, Jr.
sentences.zh: 我是马里奥·里特，小马里奥·里特。

glossary.def: a building in which interesting and valuable things (as works of art or historical or scientific objects) are collected and shown to the public artifact – n. a usually simple object (as a tool or ornament) showing human work and representing a culture or a stage in the development of a culture vision – n. a thought, idea, or object formed by the imagination dedicate – v. to set apart for some purpose and especially a sacred or serious purpose oratory – n. the job of making speeches in public
